rule: good. the rule line is never parsed; the second sentence carries it cleanly, and the other three state its new-moon, full-moon and half-moon cases — two of them needing the per-occasion fix noted below.
texts: bad: "keeps its potency" loses the "its" — potency is recorded as a bare kind with no link back to that salt-bloom — and the parse also adds a continuation ("still") the sentence never states. Say it with the adjective instead, exactly as the twin sentence that parsed cleanly does: "When a Keeper harvests salt-bloom at the new moon, that salt-bloom stays potent."

good. parses as a fireable rule — the new-moon gathering is the trigger, and the salt-bloom's staying potent is recorded both as a continuing state and as a plain "is potent" fact a later question can find.

bad: the turning is attached to the salt-bloom rather than to the gathering, so two full-moon gatherings of the same salt-bloom collapse into one turning recorded as happening during both. Everything else is right; make the per-occasion reading explicit: "Every time a Keeper gathers salt-bloom at the full moon, that salt-bloom turns to chalky residue."

mixed: the change into chalky residue and the reference back to "that salt-bloom" are recorded correctly, but the turning is again attached to the salt-bloom rather than to the gathering — the same collapse that was ruled a defect on the identical full-moon sentence — so repeated gatherings share one turning. Same fix: "Every time a Keeper gathers salt-bloom at the half moon, that salt-bloom turns to chalky residue."
